svg.aria-label: Clockwork system architecture. Triggers wake a Strands agent through run_agent: a client writes in through the public intake form, the freelancer pastes a client reply into a conversation, or a scheduler tick runs every 30 seconds locally and every 5 minutes on Vercel through a GitHub Action. The freelancer's buttons call the same twelve tools directly without the agent loop, and both paths open an agent run. Job feeds from Hacker News, Remotive and RemoteOK, plus the freelancer's GitHub and portfolio, are read by those tools. Models route by role on Groq through LiteLLM: orchestrator and reader use gpt-oss-120b, writer and extractor use gpt-oss-20b. Supabase Postgres holds accounts, profile, sourcing, conversations, deals, quotes, invoices, approvals, tasks and the full run ledger. Every step, tool call, token count and cost is written to agent_event and token_ledger and replayed in the Run Trace. Approval-gated tools have no code path that sends: they write a pending approval row, a human approves in the Approval Inbox, and only then does executor.py record the action as sent. No email is transmitted. The money tail runs quote, human acceptance, invoice, a scheduled payment check, an escalating chase, and human confirmation of payment; totals are computed in Python and no step can move money. A virtual clock routes every time read through clock.now so a demo can advance days in seconds.
svg.text: Clockwork — the business half, as a system
A Strands agent on Groq, four workflows, twelve tools, and a human approval gate. Arithmetic stays in code.
